previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, recurrent cellulitis, and chronic venous insufficiency was admitted for worsening bilateral leg pain, swelling, and serous drainage, with a history of low-grade fever and chills. Evaluation confirmed cellulitis without evidence of DVT on ultrasound. She was treated with IV vancomycin, later transitioned to oral linezolid, with clinical improvement. Her warfarin dose was increased due to a subtherapeutic INR of 1.5, and a one-time dose of torsemide was given to address increased edema. Left forearm pain was evaluated with X-ray showing advanced SLAC wrist and calcification, but no signs of acute fracture or complex regional pain syndrome. She remained stable, with negative blood cultures and improving skin findings, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics, including a plan for long-term Keflex prophylaxis, with follow-up arranged.

The patient presented with acute on chronic nausea with emesis 
and inability to tolerate PO. This has been a chronic problem

included chronic nausea from narcotic use, gastroparesis, as 
well as possible viral infection, though this was thought less 
likely, given the chronicity. There was also a concern that a 
psychosomatic component may have been contributing. The labs 
were unrevealing - chemistry, LFTS and lipase were all within 
normal limits, ruling out acute flare of pancreatitis. EKG 
similar to previous, and CXR negative for acute process. Her 
abdomen remained benign throughout the admission. Non contrast 
CT head was negative for CNS etiology of the recurrent nausea. 
She was treated symptomatically with Compazine with improvement. 
Her home oxycontin was decreased to 10 mg BID from 20 mg BID due

and she was advanced from a clear liquid diet to a regular diet 
on discharge, which she was tolerating well.

torsemide was held on admission given poor PO intake and emesis, 
but was restarted with improvement in PO intake. The patient was 
continued on home metoprolol.

The patient was thrombocytopenic to 92 on admission. In the past 
the patient has has been thrombocytopenic of unclear etiology. 
She has not been on heparin. There was concern for 
myelosuppression related to recent course of antibiotics, 
specifically linezolid and Keflex. The differential also 
included viral infection. Platelets had dropped to a nadir of 73 
but rebounded back to 91 on discharge. Given stability, and 
marked improvement in ___ cellulitis, she was continued on
